verses.1:1: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
verses.1:2: "The LORD was fiercely angry with your fathers.
verses.1:3: And you shall say to them, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Return to Me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.'
verses.1:4: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the earlier prophets called out, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Turn back now from your evil ways and your evil deeds.' Yet they did not listen and did not pay attention to Me, declares the LORD.
verses.1:5: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, will they live forever?
verses.1:6: Yet My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? So they turned back and said, 'Just as the LORD of hosts planned to do to us according to our ways and according to our deeds, so He has done with us.'"
verses.1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
verses.1:8: I saw during the night, and look, a man was riding on a red horse, and he was standing among the myrtle trees that were in the hollow; and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
verses.1:9: Then I said, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who spoke with me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
verses.1:10: And the man standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, "These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to walk about through the earth."
verses.1:11: So they answered the angel of the LORD standing among the myrtle trees and said, "We have walked about through the earth, and look, all the earth is settled and quiet."
verses.1:12: Then the angel of the LORD responded and said, "LORD of hosts, how long will You not show compassion to Jerusalem and to the cities of Judah, against which You have shown indignation these seventy years?"
verses.1:13: And the LORD answered the angel who spoke with me with good words, words of comfort.
verses.1:14: Then the angel who spoke with me said to me, "Proclaim, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy.
verses.1:15: And with great anger I am angry against the nations that are at ease; for I was angry only a little, yet they aided the calamity.
verses.1:16: Therefore this is what the LORD says: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion; My house will be built in it, declares the LORD of hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.'
verses.1:17: Proclaim again, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: My cities will again overflow with good things, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and will again choose Jerusalem.'"
verses.2:1: Then I raised my eyes and saw, and look, there were four horns.
verses.2:2: And I said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
verses.2:3: And the LORD showed me four artisans.
verses.2:4: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he spoke, saying, "These are the horns that scattered Judah to such an extent that no one raised his head; and these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that raised a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
verses.2:5: Then I raised my eyes and saw, and look, there was a man, and in his hand was a measuring cord.
verses.2:6: So I said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see what its width is and what its length is."
verses.2:7: And look, the angel who spoke with me was going out, and another angel was going out to meet him.
verses.2:8: And he said to him, "Run, speak to that young man, saying, 'Jerusalem will be inhabited as unwalled villages because of the abundance of people and livestock in its midst.
verses.2:9: And I will be to it, declares the LORD, a wall of fire all around, and I will be a glory in its midst.'"
verses.2:10: "Come! Come, and flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD; for I have spread you out like the four winds of the heavens, declares the LORD.
verses.2:11: Come, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
verses.2:12: For this is what the LORD of hosts says—after glory He has sent me to the nations that plunder you—"Indeed, the one who touches you touches the pupil of His eye.
verses.2:13: For look, I am waving My hand over them, and they will become plunder for their servants." And you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.
verses.2:14: "Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion! For look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares the LORD.
verses.2:15: And many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day, and they will become My people, and I will dwell in your midst." And you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
verses.2:16: And the LORD will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy ground, and will again choose Jerusalem.
verses.2:17: Keep silent, all flesh, in the presence of the LORD, for He has stirred Himself from His holy dwelling.
verses.3:1: Then He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with the Accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
verses.3:2: And the LORD said to the Accuser, "May the LORD rebuke you, Accuser, and may the LORD who chooses Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a firebrand rescued from the fire?"
verses.3:3: Now Joshua was dressed in filthy garments and was standing before the angel.
verses.3:4: And he answered and spoke to those standing before him, saying, "Take the filthy garments off him." And he said to him, "See, I have caused your iniquity to pass away from you, and I will dress you in festive robes."
verses.3:5: Then I said, "Let them place a clean turban on his head." So they placed the clean turban on his head and dressed him in garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
verses.3:6: And the angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua, saying:
verses.3:7: "This is what the LORD of hosts says: If you walk in My ways and if you keep My charge, then you yourself will both govern My house and also guard My courts, and I will give you the right to walk among these who are standing here.
verses.3:8: Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you—for they are men of a sign—for look, I am bringing My servant, Branch.
verses.3:9: For look at the stone that I have placed before Joshua: on a single stone are seven eyes. Look, I am engraving its inscription, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will take away the iniquity of that land in a single day.
verses.3:10: On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbor to come under a vine and under a fig tree."
verses.4:1: Then the angel who spoke with me returned and awakened me, like a man who is awakened from his sleep.
verses.4:2: He said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I have looked, and here is a lampstand all of gold, with its bowl on its top, and its seven lamps on it—seven and seven pipes for the lamps that are on its top.
verses.4:3: And two olive trees are beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left."
verses.4:4: Then I answered and said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these, my lord?"
verses.4:5: The angel who spoke with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
verses.4:6: Then he answered and said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: 'Not by force and not by strength, but by My Spirit,' says the LORD of hosts.
verses.4:7: Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground! And he will bring out the chief stone to shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"
verses.4:8: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.4:9: "Zerubbabel's hands have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it; and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
verses.4:10: For who has despised the day of small things? Yet these seven will rejoice when they see the plumb weight in Zerubbabel's hand—they are the eyes of the LORD, roaming across the whole earth."
verses.4:11: Then I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
verses.4:12: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What are the two branches of the olive trees that are beside the two gold conduits pouring out the gold from them?"
verses.4:13: He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
verses.4:14: And he said, "These are the two sons of fresh oil who stand beside the Lord of all the earth."
verses.5:1: Again I lifted up my eyes and looked, and there was a flying scroll.
verses.5:2: He said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits, and its width is ten cubits."
verses.5:3: Then he said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the face of the whole land; for everyone who steals will be purged on one side according to it, and everyone who swears will be purged on the other side according to it.
verses.5:4: 'I have sent it out,' declares the LORD of hosts, 'and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name; and it will lodge inside his house and consume it, along with its timbers and its stones.'"
verses.5:5: Then the angel who spoke with me came forward and said to me, "Now lift up your eyes and see what this is that is coming out."
verses.5:6: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the ephah that is coming out." And he said, "This is their appearance across the whole land."
verses.5:7: And look, a disc of lead was lifted up, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah.
verses.5:8: He said, "This is Wickedness." And he threw her into the middle of the ephah, and threw the lead weight onto its mouth.
verses.5:9: Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and there were two women coming out, and wind was in their wings; they had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the sky.
verses.5:10: Then I said to the angel who spoke with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"
verses.5:11: He said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar; and when that is prepared, it will be set down there on its base."
verses.6:1: Again I lifted up my eyes and looked, and there were four chariots coming out from between the two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
verses.6:2: The first chariot had red horses, and the second chariot had black horses;
verses.6:3: and the third chariot had white horses, and the fourth chariot had dappled, strong horses.
verses.6:4: Then I answered and said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these, my lord?"
verses.6:5: The angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.
verses.6:6: The one with the black horses is going out to the land of the north, and the white ones have gone out after them, and the dappled ones have gone out to the land of the south."
verses.6:7: And the strong ones went out and sought to go and range through the earth. Then He said, "Go, range through the earth." So they ranged through the earth.
verses.6:8: Then He called out to me and spoke to me, saying, "Look, those going out to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north."
verses.6:9: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.6:10: "Take from the exiles, from Heldai, from Tobijah, and from Jedaiah; and you yourself go on that day and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, where they have come from Babylon.
verses.6:11: And take silver and gold and make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
verses.6:12: Then speak to him, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Look, a man—Branch is his name—and from his own place he will branch out, and he will build the temple of the LORD.
verses.6:13: And he himself will build the temple of the LORD, and he himself will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and a priest will be on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.'
verses.6:14: And the crowns will be for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen the son of Zephaniah as a memorial in the temple of the LORD.
verses.6:15: And those who are far away will come and build on the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. And this will happen if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God."
verses.7:1: Now it happened in the fourth year of King Darius that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Kislev.
verses.7:2: And Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to implore the favor of the LORD,
verses.7:3: to speak to the priests who belonged to the house of the LORD of hosts and to the prophets, saying, "Should I weep in the fifth month, abstaining as I have done these many years?"
verses.7:4: And the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,
verses.7:5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'When you fasted and lamented in the fifth and in the seventh months for these seventy years, did you truly fast for Me, even Me?
verses.7:6: And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you who are eating and you who are drinking?
verses.7:7: Should you not hear the words that the LORD proclaimed through the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, along with its cities around it, and when the Negev and the lowland were inhabited?'"
verses.7:8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying:
verses.7:9: This is what the LORD of hosts has said, saying, "Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion, each man with his brother.
verses.7:10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the resident alien or the poor, and do not devise evil in your hearts, each man against his brother."
verses.7:11: Yet they refused to pay attention; they turned a rebellious shoulder and made their ears heavy so as not to hear.
verses.7:12: They made their hearts like diamond so as not to hear the law and the words that the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
verses.7:13: And it happened that just as He called and they did not listen, "so they would call and I would not listen," said the LORD of hosts,
verses.7:14: "and I scattered them as in a storm among all the nations that they had not known." So the land became desolate behind them, with no one passing through or returning; thus they turned a desirable land into a desolation.
verses.8:1: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came, saying:
verses.8:2: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and with great fury I am jealous for her."
verses.8:3: This is what the LORD says: "I have returned to Zion and will reside within Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts, the Mountain of Holiness."
verses.8:4: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "Old men and old women will once again sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand because of his many days.
verses.8:5: And the squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in its squares."
verses.8:6: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "If it seems too extraordinary in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be too extraordinary in My eyes?" declares the LORD of hosts.
verses.8:7: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "Look, I am saving My people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting of the sun,
verses.8:8: and I will bring them, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. They will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them, in truth and in righteousness."
verses.8:9: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "Let your hands be strong, you who in these days are hearing these words from the mouth of the prophets who were there on the day the house of the LORD of hosts had its foundation laid, for the temple to be built.
verses.8:10: For before those days there was no wage for man and no wage for animal, and for the one going out or the one coming in there was no peace from the adversary, and I set all people loose, each man against his neighbor.
verses.8:11: But now I am not toward the remnant of this people as in the former days," declares the LORD of hosts.
verses.8:12: "For it will be a sowing of peace: the vine will yield its fruit, the land will yield its produce, and the heavens will yield their dew, and I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.
verses.8:13: And it will come about that just as you have been a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong."
verses.8:14: For this is what the LORD of hosts says: "Just as I purposed to do harm to you when your fathers provoked Me to wrath," says the LORD of hosts, "and I did not relent,
verses.8:15: so I have purposed again in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
verses.8:16: These are the things that you are to do: speak truth, each man with his neighbor; judge with truth and the justice of peace in your gates.
verses.8:17: And do not devise evil in your hearts, each man against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath; for all these are things that I hate," declares the LORD.
verses.8:18: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying:
verses.8:19: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become for the house of Judah joy and gladness and happy festivals; therefore love truth and peace."
verses.8:20: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "It will yet be that peoples and the inhabitants of many cities will come.
verses.8:21: The inhabitants of one city will go to another, saying, 'Let us surely go to implore the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts; I too will go.'
verses.8:22: So many peoples and powerful nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem and to implore the favor of the LORD."
verses.8:23: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "In those days ten men from every language of the nations will take hold, yes, they will grasp the edge of a Jewish man's garment, saying, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
verses.9:1: A pronouncement: the word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place, for the eye of mankind and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD,
verses.9:2: and also Hamath, which borders on it, and Tyre and Sidon, though she is very wise.
verses.9:3: Tyre built a fortification for herself and piled up silver like dust, and fine gold like the mire of the streets.
verses.9:4: Look, the Lord will dispossess her and strike down her wealth in the sea, and she herself will be devoured by fire.
verses.9:5: Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza too, and she will writhe greatly; and Ekron as well, for her expectation has been put to shame. A king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
verses.9:6: A mixed population will dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
verses.9:7: I will remove its blood from its mouth and its detestable things from between its teeth. It too will remain for our God; it will become like a clan in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.
verses.9:8: Then I will encamp around My house as a guard against anyone passing through or returning, and no oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with My own eyes.
verses.9:9: Exult greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout out, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you; righteous and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the foal of a female donkey.
verses.9:10: And I will cut off chariotry from Ephraim and horses from Jerusalem, and the war bow will be cut off. He will speak peace to the nations; his rule will extend from sea to sea, and from the River to the farthest bounds of the earth.
verses.9:11: As for you as well, because of the blood of your covenant, I have released your prisoners from a pit that has no water in it.
verses.9:12: Return to a stronghold, you prisoners of hope! Today as well I declare that I will repay double to you.
verses.9:13: For I have bent Judah for Myself as a bow and filled it with Ephraim; I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like the sword of a mighty warrior.
verses.9:14: Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will go forth like lightning; the Lord GOD will sound the ram's horn and march in the storms of the south.
verses.9:15: The LORD of hosts will shield them; they will devour and trample down sling stones, and they will drink and clamor as with wine, and be filled like the sacrificial bowl, like the corners of an altar.
verses.9:16: On that day the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people, for they are jewels of a crown gleaming upon His land.
verses.9:17: For how great His goodness is, and how great His beauty! Grain will cause the young men to flourish, and new wine the young women.
verses.10:1: Ask the LORD for rain in the time of the late rain. The LORD makes thunderclouds, and He will give them heavy rain showers, vegetation in the field for each one.
verses.10:2: For the household idols speak wickedness, and the diviners see falsehood; they tell empty dreams and comfort with vanity. Therefore they wander away like a flock; they suffer affliction because there is no shepherd.
verses.10:3: "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will call the male goats to account; for the LORD of hosts has attended to His flock, the house of Judah, and will make them like His majestic steed in battle.
verses.10:4: From them will come the cornerstone, from them the tent peg, from them the war bow; from them every commander will go forth, all together.
verses.10:5: They will be like mighty warriors trampling in the mud of the streets in battle; and they will fight because the LORD is with them, and those who ride horses will be brought to shame.
verses.10:6: I will make the house of Judah strong, and the house of Joseph I will save; I will restore them, because I have compassion on them, and they will be as if I had not cast them off. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
verses.10:7: Ephraim will become like a mighty warrior, and their heart will be glad as from wine; their children will see and be glad, and their heart will exult in the LORD.
verses.10:8: I will whistle for them and gather them in, because I have redeemed them; and they will multiply as they once multiplied.
verses.10:9: I will sow them among the peoples, and in distant places they will remember Me; they will live with their children and will return.
verses.10:10: I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria; I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and enough room will not be found for them.
verses.10:11: He will pass through the sea of affliction and strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up; Assyria's pride will be brought down, and Egypt's scepter will depart.
verses.10:12: And I will make them strong in the LORD, and in His name they will walk," declares the LORD.
verses.11:1: Open your doors, Lebanon, so that fire may consume your cedars.
verses.11:2: Wail, cypress, because the cedar has fallen, because the majestic ones have been laid waste. Wail, oaks of Bashan, because the dense forest has come down.
verses.11:3: The sound of the wailing of the shepherds, for their majesty has been laid waste! The sound of the roaring of young lions, for the pride of the Jordan has been laid waste!
verses.11:4: This is what the LORD my God says: "Shepherd the flock of slaughter,
verses.11:5: whose buyers slaughter them and incur no guilt, and each of their sellers says, 'Blessed be the LORD, for I have grown rich!' And their shepherds have no pity on them.
verses.11:6: For I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land," declares the LORD. "Look, I am about to hand people over, each one into the hand of his neighbor and into the hand of his king; they will shatter the land, and I will not rescue them from their hand."
verses.11:7: So I shepherded the flock of slaughter—indeed, the afflicted of the flock. I took for myself two staffs: the one I named Favor, and the other I named Bonds; and I shepherded the flock.
verses.11:8: And I cut off the three shepherds in one month; my soul grew impatient with them, and their soul also detested me.
verses.11:9: Then I said, "I will not shepherd you. What is dying, let it die; what is being cut off, let it be cut off; and as for those that remain, let each one eat the flesh of another."
verses.11:10: And I took my staff Favor and snapped it in two, to annul my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
verses.11:11: It was annulled on that day, and thus the afflicted of the flock who were observing me knew that it was the word of the LORD.
verses.11:12: Then I said to them, "If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; and if not, refrain." So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
verses.11:13: And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter—the majestic price at which I was prized by them!" So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
verses.11:14: Then I snapped my second staff, Bonds, in two, to annul the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
verses.11:15: And the LORD said to me, "Once more, take for yourself the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
verses.11:16: For look, I am about to raise up a shepherd in the land: he will not attend to those being cut off, he will not search for the young, he will not heal the injured, and he will not sustain the one standing firm; rather, he will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
verses.11:17: Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! A sword against his arm and against his right eye! His arm will completely wither, and his right eye will grow utterly dim!"
verses.12:1: The pronouncement of the word of the LORD concerning Israel—the declaration of the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, founds the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
verses.12:2: "Look, I am about to make Jerusalem a bowl of staggering for all the peoples around; and it will also be against Judah during the siege against Jerusalem.
verses.12:3: And it will happen on that day that I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples; all who lift it will be severely gashed. And all the nations of the earth will be gathered against it.
verses.12:4: On that day," declares the LORD, "I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. Upon the house of Judah I will open My eyes, while I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
verses.12:5: Then the chiefs of Judah will say in their heart, 'The inhabitants of Jerusalem are a strength to me in the LORD of hosts, their God.'
verses.12:6: On that day I will make the chiefs of Judah like a brazier of fire among wood and like a torch of fire among sheaves; they will devour all the surrounding peoples to the right and to the left, while Jerusalem will again dwell in its own place, in Jerusalem.
verses.12:7: And the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the splendor of the house of David and the splendor of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will not surpass that of Judah.
verses.12:8: On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem; the one who stumbles among them on that day will become like David, and the house of David like God, like the angel of the LORD before them.
verses.12:9: And it will happen on that day that I will seek to wipe out all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
verses.12:10: And I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplications. They will look to Me, whom they have pierced, and they will mourn over Him as in mourning for an only son, and grieve bitterly over Him as in bitter grief for a firstborn.
verses.12:11: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will grow great, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.12:12: And the land will mourn, each clan apart: the clan of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the clan of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
verses.12:13: the clan of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the clan of the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart;
verses.12:14: all the clans that remain, each clan apart, and their wives apart."
verses.13:1: On that day there will be a spring opened for the house of David and for the residents of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.
verses.13:2: "And it will happen on that day," declares the LORD of hosts, "that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will not be remembered again; and I will also take away the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness from the land."
verses.13:3: And it will happen that if a man still prophesies, his father and his mother who brought him forth will say to him, "You must not live, because you have spoken falsehood in the name of the LORD." And his father and his mother who brought him forth will pierce him through while he prophesies.
verses.13:4: And it will happen on that day that the prophets will be ashamed, each man of his vision when he prophesies, and they will not wear a cloak of hair so as to deceive.
verses.13:5: And he will say, "I am not a prophet; I am a man who works the ground, for a man sold me from my youth."
verses.13:6: And someone will say to him, "What are these wounds between your hands?" Then he will say, "Those with which I was struck in the house of those who love me."
verses.13:7: "Awake, sword, against My shepherd, and against the man, My companion," declares the LORD of hosts. "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter, and I will turn back My hand against the little ones.
verses.13:8: And it will happen in all the land," declares the LORD, "that two-thirds in it will be cut off and perish, and the third part will be left in it.
verses.13:9: And I will bring the third part into the fire, and I will refine them as one refines silver, and I will test them as one tests gold. They will call on My name, and I Myself will answer them. I will say, 'They are My people,' and they in turn will say, 'The LORD is my God.'"
verses.14:1: Look, a day is coming for the LORD, when your plunder will be divided within you.
verses.14:2: And I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for war, and the city will be captured, the houses will be ransacked, and the women will be violated; and half of the city will go out into exile, but the remainder of the people will not be cut off from the city.
verses.14:3: Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as on the day of His fighting on a day of battle.
verses.14:4: And His feet will stand on that day on the Mount of Olives, which faces Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split down its center eastward and westward into a very great valley, and half of the mountain will move northward and half of it southward.
verses.14:5: And you will flee by the valley of My mountains, for the valley of the mountains will reach to Azal; and you will flee just as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with You.
verses.14:6: And it will happen on that day that there will be no light, bright splendors, or freezing.
verses.14:7: And it will be a single day, which is known to the LORD, not day and not night; and it will happen that at evening time there will be light.
verses.14:8: And it will happen on that day that living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it to the eastern sea and half of it to the western sea; in summer and in winter it will happen.
verses.14:9: And the LORD will become king over the whole earth; on that day the LORD will be one, and His name will be one.
verses.14:10: The entire land will be turned into a plain, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will rise high and remain in its place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the site of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the winepresses of the king.
verses.14:11: And people will dwell in it, and there will never again be a ban of destruction, and Jerusalem will dwell in safety.
verses.14:12: And this will be the plague by which the LORD will strike all the peoples who marched to war against Jerusalem: their flesh will decay while they stand on their feet, their eyes will decay in their sockets, and their tongues will decay in their mouths.
verses.14:13: And it will happen on that day that a great panic from the LORD will be among them, and each man will seize the hand of his companion, and his hand will rise up against the hand of his companion.
verses.14:14: And Judah too will fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations all around will be gathered up, gold and silver and clothing in very great abundance.
verses.14:15: And likewise will be the plague on the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey, and all the livestock that will be in those camps, just like this plague.
verses.14:16: And it will happen that everyone left from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
verses.14:17: And it will happen that whichever of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts, on them there will be no rain.
verses.14:18: And if the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, then on them there will be none; there will be the plague by which the LORD will strike the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
verses.14:19: This will be the penalty of Egypt, and the penalty of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
verses.14:20: On that day there will be on the bells of the horses, "Holy to the LORD." And the pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar.
verses.14:21: And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to the LORD of hosts, and all who sacrifice will come and take from them and boil in them. And there will never again be a merchant in the house of the LORD of hosts on that day.

notes.1:4: The ketiv reads a longer orthographic form with an extra yod (um'alileikhem); the qere reads uma'alleleikhem ("and your deeds"), the regular plural of ma'alal with a 2mp suffix, which is translated here.
notes.1:8: Hebrew metsulah normally refers to a depth (often of water) and here designates a low-lying hollow or glen; seruqqim ("sorrel") occurs only here as a horse color and denotes a reddish-brown or chestnut hue.
notes.1:15: Literally "they helped for evil/calamity" (azeru lera'ah), an idiom meaning that the nations exceeded God's intended discipline and intensified Judah's disaster.
notes.1:16: The ketiv reads the older spelling qaweh (cf. 1 Kgs 7:23; Jer 31:39); the qere reads the standard form qaw ("a measuring line"), which is translated here.
notes.2:4: The clause kefi-ish lo-nasa rosho is idiomatic (literally "according to the measure that no man raised his head"); leyaddot ("to cast down") is the Piel infinitive construct of yadah II ("throw/cast").
notes.2:10: The interjection hoy (doubled here and repeated in 2:11) functions as an urgent summons to attention and flight rather than a lament; the preposition ke literally means "like" ("like the four winds of the heavens").
notes.2:12: The elliptical phrase achar kavod literally means "after glory" (variously understood as "for the sake of glory," "in pursuit of glory," or "after the glory"). The hapax legomenon bavah ("pupil") denotes the delicate center of the eye; Masoretic tradition lists eino ("His eye") among the scribal emendations (Tiqqune Sopherim) for "My eye," and the speaker alternates between the sent messenger (here and at the ends of 2:13, 2:15) and the LORD.
notes.2:17: The verb ne'or is the Niphal perfect of ur ("to awake/rouse oneself"), portraying the LORD stirring Himself to act from His heavenly dwelling.
notes.3:1: Hebrew ha-satan ("the Accuser" or "the Adversary") carries the definite article as a courtroom title and forms a cognate wordplay with the Qal infinitive construct lesitno ("to accuse him").
notes.3:4: Hebrew wehalbesh is a Hiphil infinitive absolute of labash ("to clothe/dress") continuing the preceding finite verb he'evarti (Hiphil perfect of avar, literally "I have caused to pass away"); machalatsot denotes costly or festive robes (elsewhere only in Isa 3:22).
notes.3:7: The rare form mahlekim is variously parsed as the plural of mahalak ("walkways/rights of access") or an Aramaizing Hiphil participle of halak ("ones who walk"), granting Joshua access among the heavenly attendants.
notes.3:8: Hebrew tsemach ("Branch" or "Sprout") lacks the definite article and functions here as a title or proper name (cf. 6:12).
notes.4:2: Translated from the Qere וָאֹמַר ("and I said," 1cs); the Ketiv reads ויאמר ("and he said," 3ms). The distributive phrase שִׁבְעָה וְשִׁבְעָה מוּצָקוֹת ("seven and seven pipes") likely denotes seven pipes for each of the seven lamps, or fourteen pipes in total.
notes.4:7: הָאֶבֶן הָרֹאשָׁה uses the rare feminine form רֹאשָׁה (from רֹאשׁ, "head/first/top"), literally "the stone, the head/chief one," referring either to the crowning capstone that completes the temple or to its premier stone.
notes.4:10: הָאֶבֶן הַבְּדִיל is literally "the stone, the tin," denoting a tin plumb weight or plummet (or a ceremonial metal stone). Following the Masoretic accentuation, שִׁבְעָה־אֵלֶּה ("these seven") serves as the subject of וְשָׂמְחוּ וְרָאוּ ("will rejoice when they see").
notes.4:12: צַנְתְּרוֹת is a biblical hapax legomenon denoting conduits or pipes, and הַזָּהָב is literally "the gold," referring poetically to golden olive oil.
notes.4:14: בְּנֵי־הַיִּצְהָר is literally "sons of the fresh oil," a Hebrew idiom for figures consecrated with or characterized by fresh olive oil, commonly understood as anointed ones.
notes.5:3: מִזֶּה ... מִזֶּה idiomatically means "on one side ... on the other side" (the two sides of the scroll), כָּמוֹהָ ("according to it") refers to the curse, and Niphal נִקָּה (from נקה) carries the sense "be purged/cleaned out" (cf. Isa 3:26) rather than "be acquitted."
notes.5:6: הָאֵיפָה ("the ephah") is a dry measuring vessel of roughly 22 liters. Masoretic עֵינָם (lit. "their eye") is used idiomatically for "their appearance/aspect" (cf. Lev 13:55; Num 11:7), whereas the Septuagint and Syriac reflect a variant Hebrew reading עֲוֹנָם ("their iniquity").
notes.5:11: וְהוּכַן (Hophal of כּוּן) is masculine singular, referring to the בַיִת ("house"), whereas וְהֻנִּיחָה (Hophal of נוּחַ) and מְכֻנָתָהּ ("its base/pedestal," also from כּוּן) are feminine singular, referring to the ephah.
notes.6:3: אֲמֻצִּים (also in 6:7) derives from the root אמץ ("be strong") yet follows the Hebrew color-adjective pattern (like אֲדֻמִּים "red" and בְּרֻדִּים "dappled"), leading some scholars to understand it as a horse color such as "bay" or "sorrel."
notes.6:5: Hebrew רוּחוֹת can mean either "winds" (matching the four compass directions, cf. Zech 2:6) or "spirits" (matching their standing in the heavenly court before God, cf. Ps 104:4).
notes.6:12: צֶמַח ("Branch") and יִצְמָח ("will branch out") play on the root צמח, literally "sprout/shoot" and "sprout up"; מִתַּחְתָּיו is literally "from beneath him," an idiom for "from his own place."
notes.6:13: וְהָיָה כֹהֵן עַל־כִּסְאוֹ is syntactically ambiguous in Hebrew and may be read either as "a priest will be on his throne" (a second figure beside the royal Branch, matching "between the two of them") or as "he will be a priest on his throne" (uniting royal and priestly roles in one figure).
notes.6:14: Plural הָעֲטָרֹת ("the crowns," as in 6:11) takes a feminine singular verb תִּהְיֶה, indicating either a single composite crown or collective crowns. חֵלֶם ("Helem") and חֵן ("Hen," also possibly the common noun "graciousness") correspond to Heldai and Josiah in 6:10.
notes.7:2: In the Masoretic accentuation, Bethel is the subject ("Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men"), though some construe Bethel-sharezer as a single Babylonian personal name or read Bethel as the destination. The idiom translated "implore the favor of" literally means "appease/soften the face of" (Piel of chalah).
notes.7:7: The Hebrew begins with the interrogative particle and direct-object marker (halo et-haddevarim) without an expressed verb, implying a verb such as "hear" or "heed"; alternatively, et may function as an emphatic subject marker ("Are these not the words...").
notes.7:14: The Hebrew verb rendered "I scattered them as in a storm" is an unusual imperfect form from sa'ar ("whirl/storm away"), used here in context for the past exile that left the land desolate.
notes.8:6: The Niphal verb (yippale, from pala) denotes what is extraordinary, marvelous, or beyond human ability, and the second clause functions as an unmarked rhetorical question.
notes.8:12: The opening clause literally reads "for a sowing/seed of peace" without an expressed verb, introducing the threefold promise of agricultural abundance.
notes.8:17: The Hebrew combines the direct-object marker (et) with the relative pronoun (asher) before "I hate" (ki et-kol-elleh asher saneti), an emphatic Late Biblical Hebrew construction.
notes.9:1: The Masoretic Hebrew literally reads "for to/toward the LORD is the eye of mankind and all the tribes of Israel," indicating either that humanity and Israel look toward the LORD or that His watchful attention encompasses them.
notes.9:8: The Hebrew mitstsava (a rare form related to matstsava, "garrison/guard") is rendered "as a guard"; some revocalize it as min-tsava ("against an army/host").
notes.9:9: The word rendered "victorious" is a Niphal participle (nosha, from yasha), literally "saved" or "delivered," indicating that the king is granted deliverance and victory by God.
notes.9:15: Following the Masoretic Hebrew literally ("sling stones" and "as with wine"); the closing simile evokes the mizraq, the temple basin used for dashing sacrificial blood onto the corners of the altar.
notes.9:17: The third-person masculine singular suffixes on "goodness" and "beauty" may refer to the LORD (compare Jeremiah 31:12, where the LORD's goodness yields grain and new wine) or collectively to His people in verse 16.
notes.10:3: Hebrew uses the same verb paqad in two opposite senses: with the preposition al ("call to account" or "punish") and with the direct object marker et ("attend to" or "care for"). "Male goats" (attudim) is a Hebrew metaphor for flock leaders.
notes.10:4: Hebrew uses the masculine singular pronoun mimmennu ("from it" or "from him"), referring collectively to the house of Judah in v. 3. The Qal participle noges normally means "taskmaster" or "oppressor," but here denotes an authoritative commander or ruler.
notes.10:6: The verb wehoshbotim is a rare mixed Hebrew form blending the Hiphil of yashav ("settle" or "cause to dwell") and the Hiphil of shuv ("bring back" or "restore," cf. v. 10).
notes.10:11: Hebrew bayyam tsarah literally reads "through the sea, affliction," an appositional construction meaning "the sea of affliction" or "distress." The third-person masculine singular verbs ("He will pass... strike") have the LORD as subject.
notes.11:2: Ketiv reads habbatsur (Qal passive participle of batsar, "fortified" or "inaccessible"), while Qere reads the adjective habbatsir ("impenetrable" or "dense"); both describe a thick, impenetrable forest.
notes.11:7: Following the Masoretic Text laken aniyye hattson ("indeed, the afflicted of the flock"; cf. v. 11). The Septuagint redivides the consonants to read "for the sheep merchants."
notes.11:13: The Masoretic Text clearly reads hayyotser (Qal participle of yatsar, "the potter"). Some ancient versions (e.g. the Syriac) reflect ha'otsar ("the treasury") instead.
notes.11:16: Hebrew hanna'ar normally means "the young" (collectively, the young of the flock). Some interpreters instead connect the word to the verb na'ar ("shake out") and render it "the scattered" or "straying."
notes.11:17: The final -i on ro'i ("shepherd") and ozevi ("who deserts") is the archaic poetic linking vowel (hireq compaginis) rather than the first-person possessive suffix "my."
notes.12:2: The Hebrew clause literally reads "and also upon Judah it will be in the siege against Jerusalem," which may mean either that Judah too will be caught in the siege or that Judah will be forced into the siege against Jerusalem.
notes.12:5: Hebrew allufe ("chiefs" or "leaders"; also in v. 6) can alternatively be rendered "clans." The singular pronoun li ("to me") is distributive, representing each leader's inner thought.
notes.12:10: The Masoretic Text reads elay ("to Me") with et asher-daqaru ("whom they have pierced") and then shifts to the third-person pronoun alav ("over Him"). The form wehamer is a Hiphil infinitive absolute of marar ("grieve bitterly") continuing the preceding finite verb.
notes.12:11: The construct phrase "mourning of Hadad-rimmon" may refer either to lamentation at a place named Hadad-rimmon (often linked to King Josiah's death, 2 Chr 35:22-25) or to ritual mourning for a deity of that name. Hebrew spells Megiddo here as Megiddon.
notes.13:5: Hebrew hiqnani is a unique Hiphil perfect of qanah ("acquire, buy"), here understood causatively as "sold me" (transferred ownership of me), though some render it "acquired me" or "made me possess [land]."
notes.13:6: Hebrew ben yadekha literally means "between your hands," an idiom likely referring to the chest or upper back; me'ahavay is a Piel participle of ahav ("those who love me").
notes.13:8: Hebrew pi-shenayim literally means "a portion of two," here denoting two-thirds in contrast to hashelishit ("the third part").
notes.14:2: Ketiv reads tishshagalnah (Niphal imperfect of shagal, a coarser verb for sexual assault); Qere substitutes the euphemistic Niphal imperfect tishshakhavnah (from shakhav, "be lain with," i.e., "be violated").
notes.14:5: MT reads wenastem ("and you will flee," Qal perfect of nus) twice, matching nastem ("you fled"); ancient versions such as the Septuagint read a Niphal of satam ("will be blocked"). Note also the abrupt person shifts in MT from "My mountains" (the LORD speaking) to "my God" and "with You" (the prophet addressing the LORD).
notes.14:6: A difficult Hebrew text: MT reads yeqarot ("bright/precious things," likely celestial lights, cf. Job 31:26) followed by Qere weqippa'on ("and/or freezing/congealing," a noun from qafa'); Ketiv reads the Qal imperfect verb yiqpa'un ("they will congeal/dwindle").
notes.14:18: MT places the major disjunctive accent on welo alehem ("and not on them"), elliptically echoing "no rain" from v. 17 since Egypt relied on the Nile rather than rain; some read welo as a rhetorical question ("will not the plague be on them?").
notes.14:21: Hebrew kena'ani literally means "Canaanite," but is also used idiomatically in Biblical Hebrew for "merchant" or "trader" (cf. Prov 31:24), fitting the temple-vessel context of vv. 20-21.

native_verses.1:1: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
native_verses.1:2: "The LORD was fiercely angry with your fathers.
native_verses.1:3: And you shall say to them, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Return to Me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.'
native_verses.1:4: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the earlier prophets called out, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Turn back now from your evil ways and your evil deeds.' Yet they did not listen and did not pay attention to Me, declares the LORD.
native_verses.1:5: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, will they live forever?
native_verses.1:6: Yet My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? So they turned back and said, 'Just as the LORD of hosts planned to do to us according to our ways and according to our deeds, so He has done with us.'"
native_verses.1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
native_verses.1:8: I saw during the night, and look, a man was riding on a red horse, and he was standing among the myrtle trees that were in the hollow; and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
native_verses.1:9: Then I said, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who spoke with me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
native_verses.1:10: And the man standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, "These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to walk about through the earth."
native_verses.1:11: So they answered the angel of the LORD standing among the myrtle trees and said, "We have walked about through the earth, and look, all the earth is settled and quiet."
native_verses.1:12: Then the angel of the LORD responded and said, "LORD of hosts, how long will You not show compassion to Jerusalem and to the cities of Judah, against which You have shown indignation these seventy years?"
native_verses.1:13: And the LORD answered the angel who spoke with me with good words, words of comfort.
native_verses.1:14: Then the angel who spoke with me said to me, "Proclaim, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy.
native_verses.1:15: And with great anger I am angry against the nations that are at ease; for I was angry only a little, yet they aided the calamity.
native_verses.1:16: Therefore this is what the LORD says: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion; My house will be built in it, declares the LORD of hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.'
native_verses.1:17: Proclaim again, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: My cities will again overflow with good things, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and will again choose Jerusalem.'"
native_verses.2:1: Then I raised my eyes and saw, and look, there were four horns.
native_verses.2:2: And I said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
native_verses.2:3: And the LORD showed me four artisans.
native_verses.2:4: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he spoke, saying, "These are the horns that scattered Judah to such an extent that no one raised his head; and these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that raised a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
native_verses.2:5: Then I raised my eyes and saw, and look, there was a man, and in his hand was a measuring cord.
native_verses.2:6: So I said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see what its width is and what its length is."
native_verses.2:7: And look, the angel who spoke with me was going out, and another angel was going out to meet him.
native_verses.2:8: And he said to him, "Run, speak to that young man, saying, 'Jerusalem will be inhabited as unwalled villages because of the abundance of people and livestock in its midst.
native_verses.2:9: And I will be to it, declares the LORD, a wall of fire all around, and I will be a glory in its midst.'"
native_verses.2:10: "Come! Come, and flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD; for I have spread you out like the four winds of the heavens, declares the LORD.
native_verses.2:11: Come, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
native_verses.2:12: For this is what the LORD of hosts says—after glory He has sent me to the nations that plunder you—"Indeed, the one who touches you touches the pupil of His eye.
native_verses.2:13: For look, I am waving My hand over them, and they will become plunder for their servants." And you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.
native_verses.2:14: "Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion! For look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares the LORD.
native_verses.2:15: And many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day, and they will become My people, and I will dwell in your midst." And you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
native_verses.2:16: And the LORD will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy ground, and will again choose Jerusalem.
native_verses.2:17: Keep silent, all flesh, in the presence of the LORD, for He has stirred Himself from His holy dwelling.
native_verses.3:1: Then He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with the Accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
native_verses.3:2: And the LORD said to the Accuser, "May the LORD rebuke you, Accuser, and may the LORD who chooses Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a firebrand rescued from the fire?"
native_verses.3:3: Now Joshua was dressed in filthy garments and was standing before the angel.
native_verses.3:4: And he answered and spoke to those standing before him, saying, "Take the filthy garments off him." And he said to him, "See, I have caused your iniquity to pass away from you, and I will dress you in festive robes."
native_verses.3:5: Then I said, "Let them place a clean turban on his head." So they placed the clean turban on his head and dressed him in garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
native_verses.3:6: And the angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua, saying:
native_verses.3:7: "This is what the LORD of hosts says: If you walk in My ways and if you keep My charge, then you yourself will both govern My house and also guard My courts, and I will give you the right to walk among these who are standing here.
native_verses.3:8: Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you—for they are men of a sign—for look, I am bringing My servant, Branch.
native_verses.3:9: For look at the stone that I have placed before Joshua: on a single stone are seven eyes. Look, I am engraving its inscription, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will take away the iniquity of that land in a single day.
native_verses.3:10: On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbor to come under a vine and under a fig tree."
native_verses.4:1: Then the angel who spoke with me returned and awakened me, like a man who is awakened from his sleep.
native_verses.4:2: He said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I have looked, and here is a lampstand all of gold, with its bowl on its top, and its seven lamps on it—seven and seven pipes for the lamps that are on its top.
native_verses.4:3: And two olive trees are beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left."
native_verses.4:4: Then I answered and said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these, my lord?"
native_verses.4:5: The angel who spoke with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
native_verses.4:6: Then he answered and said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: 'Not by force and not by strength, but by My Spirit,' says the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.4:7: Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground! And he will bring out the chief stone to shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"
native_verses.4:8: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.4:9: "Zerubbabel's hands have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it; and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
native_verses.4:10: For who has despised the day of small things? Yet these seven will rejoice when they see the plumb weight in Zerubbabel's hand—they are the eyes of the LORD, roaming across the whole earth."
native_verses.4:11: Then I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
native_verses.4:12: And I answered a second time and said to him, "What are the two branches of the olive trees that are beside the two gold conduits pouring out the gold from them?"
native_verses.4:13: He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
native_verses.4:14: And he said, "These are the two sons of fresh oil who stand beside the Lord of all the earth."
native_verses.5:1: Again I lifted up my eyes and looked, and there was a flying scroll.
native_verses.5:2: He said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits, and its width is ten cubits."
native_verses.5:3: Then he said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the face of the whole land; for everyone who steals will be purged on one side according to it, and everyone who swears will be purged on the other side according to it.
native_verses.5:4: 'I have sent it out,' declares the LORD of hosts, 'and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name; and it will lodge inside his house and consume it, along with its timbers and its stones.'"
native_verses.5:5: Then the angel who spoke with me came forward and said to me, "Now lift up your eyes and see what this is that is coming out."
native_verses.5:6: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the ephah that is coming out." And he said, "This is their appearance across the whole land."
native_verses.5:7: And look, a disc of lead was lifted up, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah.
native_verses.5:8: He said, "This is Wickedness." And he threw her into the middle of the ephah, and threw the lead weight onto its mouth.
native_verses.5:9: Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and there were two women coming out, and wind was in their wings; they had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the sky.
native_verses.5:10: Then I said to the angel who spoke with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"
native_verses.5:11: He said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar; and when that is prepared, it will be set down there on its base."
native_verses.6:1: Again I lifted up my eyes and looked, and there were four chariots coming out from between the two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
native_verses.6:2: The first chariot had red horses, and the second chariot had black horses;
native_verses.6:3: and the third chariot had white horses, and the fourth chariot had dappled, strong horses.
native_verses.6:4: Then I answered and said to the angel who spoke with me, "What are these, my lord?"
native_verses.6:5: The angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.
native_verses.6:6: The one with the black horses is going out to the land of the north, and the white ones have gone out after them, and the dappled ones have gone out to the land of the south."
native_verses.6:7: And the strong ones went out and sought to go and range through the earth. Then He said, "Go, range through the earth." So they ranged through the earth.
native_verses.6:8: Then He called out to me and spoke to me, saying, "Look, those going out to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north."
native_verses.6:9: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
native_verses.6:10: "Take from the exiles, from Heldai, from Tobijah, and from Jedaiah; and you yourself go on that day and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, where they have come from Babylon.
native_verses.6:11: And take silver and gold and make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
native_verses.6:12: Then speak to him, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Look, a man—Branch is his name—and from his own place he will branch out, and he will build the temple of the LORD.
native_verses.6:13: And he himself will build the temple of the LORD, and he himself will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and a priest will be on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.'
native_verses.6:14: And the crowns will be for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen the son of Zephaniah as a memorial in the temple of the LORD.
native_verses.6:15: And those who are far away will come and build on the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. And this will happen if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God."
native_verses.7:1: Now it happened in the fourth year of King Darius that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Kislev.
native_verses.7:2: And Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to implore the favor of the LORD,
native_verses.7:3: to speak to the priests who belonged to the house of the LORD of hosts and to the prophets, saying, "Should I weep in the fifth month, abstaining as I have done these many years?"
native_verses.7:4: And the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,
native_verses.7:5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'When you fasted and lamented in the fifth and in the seventh months for these seventy years, did you truly fast for Me, even Me?
native_verses.7:6: And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you who are eating and you who are drinking?
native_verses.7:7: Should you not hear the words that the LORD proclaimed through the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, along with its cities around it, and when the Negev and the lowland were inhabited?'"
native_verses.7:8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying:
native_verses.7:9: This is what the LORD of hosts has said, saying, "Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion, each man with his brother.
native_verses.7:10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the resident alien or the poor, and do not devise evil in your hearts, each man against his brother."
native_verses.7:11: Yet they refused to pay attention; they turned a rebellious shoulder and made their ears heavy so as not to hear.
native_verses.7:12: They made their hearts like diamond so as not to hear the law and the words that the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.7:13: And it happened that just as He called and they did not listen, "so they would call and I would not listen," said the LORD of hosts,
native_verses.7:14: "and I scattered them as in a storm among all the nations that they had not known." So the land became desolate behind them, with no one passing through or returning; thus they turned a desirable land into a desolation.
native_verses.8:1: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came, saying:
native_verses.8:2: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and with great fury I am jealous for her."
native_verses.8:3: This is what the LORD says: "I have returned to Zion and will reside within Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts, the Mountain of Holiness."
native_verses.8:4: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "Old men and old women will once again sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand because of his many days.
native_verses.8:5: And the squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in its squares."
native_verses.8:6: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "If it seems too extraordinary in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be too extraordinary in My eyes?" declares the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.8:7: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "Look, I am saving My people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting of the sun,
native_verses.8:8: and I will bring them, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. They will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them, in truth and in righteousness."
native_verses.8:9: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "Let your hands be strong, you who in these days are hearing these words from the mouth of the prophets who were there on the day the house of the LORD of hosts had its foundation laid, for the temple to be built.
native_verses.8:10: For before those days there was no wage for man and no wage for animal, and for the one going out or the one coming in there was no peace from the adversary, and I set all people loose, each man against his neighbor.
native_verses.8:11: But now I am not toward the remnant of this people as in the former days," declares the LORD of hosts.
native_verses.8:12: "For it will be a sowing of peace: the vine will yield its fruit, the land will yield its produce, and the heavens will yield their dew, and I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.
native_verses.8:13: And it will come about that just as you have been a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong."
native_verses.8:14: For this is what the LORD of hosts says: "Just as I purposed to do harm to you when your fathers provoked Me to wrath," says the LORD of hosts, "and I did not relent,
native_verses.8:15: so I have purposed again in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
native_verses.8:16: These are the things that you are to do: speak truth, each man with his neighbor; judge with truth and the justice of peace in your gates.
native_verses.8:17: And do not devise evil in your hearts, each man against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath; for all these are things that I hate," declares the LORD.
native_verses.8:18: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying:
native_verses.8:19: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become for the house of Judah joy and gladness and happy festivals; therefore love truth and peace."
native_verses.8:20: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "It will yet be that peoples and the inhabitants of many cities will come.
native_verses.8:21: The inhabitants of one city will go to another, saying, 'Let us surely go to implore the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts; I too will go.'
native_verses.8:22: So many peoples and powerful nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem and to implore the favor of the LORD."
native_verses.8:23: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "In those days ten men from every language of the nations will take hold, yes, they will grasp the edge of a Jewish man's garment, saying, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
native_verses.9:1: A pronouncement: the word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place, for the eye of mankind and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD,
native_verses.9:2: and also Hamath, which borders on it, and Tyre and Sidon, though she is very wise.
native_verses.9:3: Tyre built a fortification for herself and piled up silver like dust, and fine gold like the mire of the streets.
native_verses.9:4: Look, the Lord will dispossess her and strike down her wealth in the sea, and she herself will be devoured by fire.
native_verses.9:5: Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza too, and she will writhe greatly; and Ekron as well, for her expectation has been put to shame. A king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
native_verses.9:6: A mixed population will dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
native_verses.9:7: I will remove its blood from its mouth and its detestable things from between its teeth. It too will remain for our God; it will become like a clan in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.
native_verses.9:8: Then I will encamp around My house as a guard against anyone passing through or returning, and no oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with My own eyes.
native_verses.9:9: Exult greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout out, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you; righteous and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the foal of a female donkey.
native_verses.9:10: And I will cut off chariotry from Ephraim and horses from Jerusalem, and the war bow will be cut off. He will speak peace to the nations; his rule will extend from sea to sea, and from the River to the farthest bounds of the earth.
native_verses.9:11: As for you as well, because of the blood of your covenant, I have released your prisoners from a pit that has no water in it.
native_verses.9:12: Return to a stronghold, you prisoners of hope! Today as well I declare that I will repay double to you.
native_verses.9:13: For I have bent Judah for Myself as a bow and filled it with Ephraim; I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like the sword of a mighty warrior.
native_verses.9:14: Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will go forth like lightning; the Lord GOD will sound the ram's horn and march in the storms of the south.
native_verses.9:15: The LORD of hosts will shield them; they will devour and trample down sling stones, and they will drink and clamor as with wine, and be filled like the sacrificial bowl, like the corners of an altar.
native_verses.9:16: On that day the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people, for they are jewels of a crown gleaming upon His land.
native_verses.9:17: For how great His goodness is, and how great His beauty! Grain will cause the young men to flourish, and new wine the young women.
native_verses.10:1: Ask the LORD for rain in the time of the late rain. The LORD makes thunderclouds, and He will give them heavy rain showers, vegetation in the field for each one.
native_verses.10:2: For the household idols speak wickedness, and the diviners see falsehood; they tell empty dreams and comfort with vanity. Therefore they wander away like a flock; they suffer affliction because there is no shepherd.
native_verses.10:3: "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will call the male goats to account; for the LORD of hosts has attended to His flock, the house of Judah, and will make them like His majestic steed in battle.
native_verses.10:4: From them will come the cornerstone, from them the tent peg, from them the war bow; from them every commander will go forth, all together.
native_verses.10:5: They will be like mighty warriors trampling in the mud of the streets in battle; and they will fight because the LORD is with them, and those who ride horses will be brought to shame.
native_verses.10:6: I will make the house of Judah strong, and the house of Joseph I will save; I will restore them, because I have compassion on them, and they will be as if I had not cast them off. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
native_verses.10:7: Ephraim will become like a mighty warrior, and their heart will be glad as from wine; their children will see and be glad, and their heart will exult in the LORD.
native_verses.10:8: I will whistle for them and gather them in, because I have redeemed them; and they will multiply as they once multiplied.
native_verses.10:9: I will sow them among the peoples, and in distant places they will remember Me; they will live with their children and will return.
native_verses.10:10: I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria; I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and enough room will not be found for them.
native_verses.10:11: He will pass through the sea of affliction and strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up; Assyria's pride will be brought down, and Egypt's scepter will depart.
native_verses.10:12: And I will make them strong in the LORD, and in His name they will walk," declares the LORD.
native_verses.11:1: Open your doors, Lebanon, so that fire may consume your cedars.
native_verses.11:2: Wail, cypress, because the cedar has fallen, because the majestic ones have been laid waste. Wail, oaks of Bashan, because the dense forest has come down.
native_verses.11:3: The sound of the wailing of the shepherds, for their majesty has been laid waste! The sound of the roaring of young lions, for the pride of the Jordan has been laid waste!
native_verses.11:4: This is what the LORD my God says: "Shepherd the flock of slaughter,
native_verses.11:5: whose buyers slaughter them and incur no guilt, and each of their sellers says, 'Blessed be the LORD, for I have grown rich!' And their shepherds have no pity on them.
native_verses.11:6: For I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land," declares the LORD. "Look, I am about to hand people over, each one into the hand of his neighbor and into the hand of his king; they will shatter the land, and I will not rescue them from their hand."
native_verses.11:7: So I shepherded the flock of slaughter—indeed, the afflicted of the flock. I took for myself two staffs: the one I named Favor, and the other I named Bonds; and I shepherded the flock.
native_verses.11:8: And I cut off the three shepherds in one month; my soul grew impatient with them, and their soul also detested me.
native_verses.11:9: Then I said, "I will not shepherd you. What is dying, let it die; what is being cut off, let it be cut off; and as for those that remain, let each one eat the flesh of another."
native_verses.11:10: And I took my staff Favor and snapped it in two, to annul my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
native_verses.11:11: It was annulled on that day, and thus the afflicted of the flock who were observing me knew that it was the word of the LORD.
native_verses.11:12: Then I said to them, "If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; and if not, refrain." So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
native_verses.11:13: And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter—the majestic price at which I was prized by them!" So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
native_verses.11:14: Then I snapped my second staff, Bonds, in two, to annul the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
native_verses.11:15: And the LORD said to me, "Once more, take for yourself the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
native_verses.11:16: For look, I am about to raise up a shepherd in the land: he will not attend to those being cut off, he will not search for the young, he will not heal the injured, and he will not sustain the one standing firm; rather, he will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
native_verses.11:17: Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! A sword against his arm and against his right eye! His arm will completely wither, and his right eye will grow utterly dim!"
native_verses.12:1: The pronouncement of the word of the LORD concerning Israel—the declaration of the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, founds the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
native_verses.12:2: "Look, I am about to make Jerusalem a bowl of staggering for all the peoples around; and it will also be against Judah during the siege against Jerusalem.
native_verses.12:3: And it will happen on that day that I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples; all who lift it will be severely gashed. And all the nations of the earth will be gathered against it.
native_verses.12:4: On that day," declares the LORD, "I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. Upon the house of Judah I will open My eyes, while I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
native_verses.12:5: Then the chiefs of Judah will say in their heart, 'The inhabitants of Jerusalem are a strength to me in the LORD of hosts, their God.'
native_verses.12:6: On that day I will make the chiefs of Judah like a brazier of fire among wood and like a torch of fire among sheaves; they will devour all the surrounding peoples to the right and to the left, while Jerusalem will again dwell in its own place, in Jerusalem.
native_verses.12:7: And the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the splendor of the house of David and the splendor of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will not surpass that of Judah.
native_verses.12:8: On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem; the one who stumbles among them on that day will become like David, and the house of David like God, like the angel of the LORD before them.
native_verses.12:9: And it will happen on that day that I will seek to wipe out all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
native_verses.12:10: And I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplications. native_verses.12:11: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will grow great, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
native_verses.12:12: And the land will mourn, each clan apart: the clan of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the clan of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
native_verses.12:13: the clan of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the clan of the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart;

native_verses.13:2: "And it will happen on that day," declares the LORD of hosts, "that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will not be remembered again; and I will also take away the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness from the land."

native_verses.13:4: And it will happen on that day that the prophets will be ashamed, each man of his vision when he prophesies, and they will not wear a cloak of hair so as to deceive.

native_verses.13:6: And someone will say to him, "What are these wounds between your hands?" Then he will say, "Those with which I was struck in the house of those who love me."
native_verses.13:7: "Awake, sword, against My shepherd, and against the man, My companion," declares the LORD of hosts. "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter, and I will turn back My hand against the little ones.
native_verses.13:8: And it will happen in all the land," declares the LORD, "that two-thirds in it will be cut off and perish, and the third part will be left in it.
native_verses.13:9: And I will bring the third part into the fire, and I will refine them as one refines silver, and I will test them as one tests gold. They will call on My name, and I Myself will answer them. I will say, 'They are My people,' and they in turn will say, 'The LORD is my God.'"
